column1: Wicomico County Right to Farm and Commercial Seafood Operation Notice

Wicomico County recognizes and supports the right to farm agricultural lands and Commercial Seafood Operations in a manner consistent with generally accepted agricultural and Commercial Seafood management practices. Residents of property on or near agricultural land or Commercial Seafood Operations should be prepared to accept the inconveniences or discomforts associated with agricultural or Commercial Seafood Operations, including but not limited to noise, odors, flies, fumes, dust, the operation of machinery of any kind during any 24-hour period (including aircraft), vibration, the storage and disposal of manure, and the application by spraying or otherwise of chemical fertilizers, soil amendments, herbicides and pesticides. Wicomico County has determined that inconveniences or discomforts associated with such agricultural or Commercial Seafood operations shall not be considered to be an interference with reasonable use and enjoyment of land, if such operations are conducted in accordance with generally accepted agricultural or Commercial Seafood practices. Wicomico County has established an Agricultural and Commercial Seafood Operation

Reconciliation Committee to assist in the resolution of disputes which might arise between persons in this County regarding whether agricultural operations conducted on agricultural lands or Commercial Seafood Activity are causing an interference with the reasonable use and enjoyment of land or personal well being and whether those operations are being conducted in accordance with generally accepted agricultural or Commercial Seafood practices. If you have any questions concerning this policy or the Reconciliation Committee, please contact the Department of Planning, Zoning and Community Development.
